properties.rop_renaming_meaning: Sue-meg is the Yurok name for this coast, used since time immemorial. The former name honored Patrick Beegan, an 1850s settler later implicated in violence against Native Americans.
properties.description: In 2021, Sue-meg became the first site renamed under California State Parks' Reexamining Our Past initiative, restoring the Yurok place name in place of Patrick's Point.
properties.compare_source: T. T. Waterman, Yurok Geography (1920), Rectangle J

properties.description: Sumêg Village is a reconstructed Yurok plank-house village, planned and built in the 1990s by Yurok people working with local park staff. Its family houses, sweathouse, changing houses, dance house, and redwood canoe make visible a permanent-village form within a place that was used primarily as a seasonal Yurok encampment. It is a living site for teaching, ceremony, and cultural transmission.
properties.caption: Sumêg Village, rebuilt in the 1990s - a living cultural site, not a museum exhibit.

properties.description: The larger of the Turtle Rocks near Sue-meg. The Yurok Language Project records chkweges as “hair seal” and Chkweges ’W-a’aag as a sea-stack near Patrick’s Point. As an offshore named place, it marks the ocean not as empty space, but as part of a Yurok coastal geography of animals, rocks, travel, and memory.
properties.caption: “Seals’ Rock” / Turtle Rocks
